correctness.rationale: There is an independent proof on the comparison coordinates. For i<j let x_ij=1 if i is preferred to j. For i<j<k, a strict no-valley ranking forces x_ij<=x_ik<=x_jk: a violation puts the middle alternative below both extremes using transitivity. It follows that x is monotone on the triangular poset of pairs (i,j), ordered by both coordinates (first increase the right coordinate, then the left). Conversely these inequalities rule out the two cyclic orientations of every triple and also exclude the middle-worst orientation, so a monotone assignment defines a strict single-peaked ranking. A set of coordinates is shattered precisely if it is an antichain: comparable coordinates forbid labels 1 then 0, and any antichain labelling extends by taking the upset generated by its positive elements. Antichains are exactly the matchings whose left endpoints increase while right endpoints strictly decrease. A set of 2d endpoints therefore determines precisely one such support, giving the binomial coefficients, their even-part sum 2^(n-1), and VC dimension floor(n/2). Removing the actual worst endpoint of the remaining segment gives 2^(n-1) distinct rankings, and comparing the two endpoints at every node yields a complete tree of depth n-1 whose two branches both extend. The cardinality bound gives the reverse Littlestone inequality, including n=1. The frozen verifier and its output through n=9 were inspected; this correctness argument is not an extrapolation from those tests, and the verifier was not re-executed.
residual_risks: Only the specified axis, strict complete rankings, and pair-comparison queries are covered; no formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: As a mathematical classification, the result is substantive: it determines every set of fixed queries that can be varied independently, not just the largest size, and locates a sharp gap between fixed and adaptive comparisons. Those conclusions are useful for this natural preference model. This value judgment does not remove the complete overlap on originality.
residual_risks: The sharp values do not apply to changing or unknown axes, tied ballots, or different query models.
